chunks: Said the one who had knowledge of the Book: 'I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you.' When he saw it placed before him, he said: 'This is from the grace of my Lord to test me whether I am grateful or thankless. And whoever is grateful, he is grateful for himself; and whoever is ungrateful, then surely my Lord is Free of need, Generous.'

key_terms.أَشْكُرُ أَمْ أَكْفُرُ: Whether I am grateful or thankless

ai.seo_question: What did Solomon say when he received the throne of Sheba?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the 'knowledgeable one' is often identified as Asif ibn Barkhiya, who utilized the 'Great Name of God' (Ism al-A'zam) to transport the throne, highlighting the interplay between divine power and prophetic agency. Solomon’s declaration serves as a paradigm for recognizing miracles not as personal achievements but as divine tests (balā’) to distinguish between sincere gratitude (shukr) and ingratitude (kufr). This event underscores the concept that true thankfulness is an internal state of the soul that benefits the believer, while God remains independent of creation's appreciation.
